and when he perceived that he was dying,
he made his nobles swear allegiance to his young son Malik-Shah,
and sent him to Baghdad.
And Jalal al-Dawlah Malik-Shah was proclaimed Sultan,
while he was four years old.
And Barkyaruq died,
and was buried in Isfahan.
And while Malik-Shah son of Barkyaruq was in Baghdad,
Sultan Muhammad, his uncle, also came to Baghdad.
And the people of Baghdad were very much afraid
lest they be plundered in the conflict that would arise between the two of them.
And because the Amir Ayaz,
to whom the governance of his (Malik-Shah's) kingdom was entrusted,
was an intelligent man,
and all the forces of Barkyaruq were under his command and in his subjection,
he extracted a word of oath from Sultan Muhammad and said:
"This child is your brother's son,
and it is more fitting for you to care for him,
and not deprive him of the kingdom and inheritance of his father,
more than for me."
And the Sultan said:
"This is my own son,"
and promised him good things.
And the Amir Ayaz went out
to the Sultan,
and was received with honor.
And after a day,
the Amir Ayaz {OCR: Ayaz} made a banquet,
and requested the Sultan to be present at it.
And the Sultan consented and went.
And by an evil chance,
there was present in the gathering of the Amir Ayaz {OCR: Ayaz}
a certain man, a scribe, who was wearing a coat of mail underneath,
and was standing with those who were serving,
and moving with difficulty.
And when the Sultan cast his gaze upon him,
he said secretly to one of the young servants standing before him:
"Go feel that man and see what is with him,
that he is so clumsy in his going and his coming." And when that boy went as if playing,
and felt him,
he came and said to the Sultan:
"He is wearing a coat of mail inside his tunic."
And the Sultan said:
"When scribes wear coats of mail,
what then should Turkish horsemen wear?" And he suspected deceit in the heart of Ayaz.
And he commanded the guards {OCR: guards/speculatores} before him,
and they cut off his head.
Now the Turks of Ayaz {OCR: Ayaz},
when they heard this,
took what they could of their own and of others,
and fled to Syria.
